subtitle: Saffire · Game Boy

body: James Bond 007 is Saffire's Game Boy action adventure about a weapons-smuggling operation that grows into a much larger threat. The agent travels through villages, cities and hostile facilities, meeting familiar film characters including Oddjob and Jaws. Viewed from above, the journey makes room for conversation, exploration and the use of collected objects between fights. A new location can ask Bond to find information or a useful tool before confronting its guards, giving the portable mission a different rhythm from the first-person action associated with GoldenEye.

Bond carries weapons and other equipment whose purpose depends on the situation. Some problems require an object to be used at the appropriate place, while others can be handled through fists, martial arts or gunfire. The player has to investigate the surroundings rather than assume every obstacle is another target. Eleven levels provide the route through the conspiracy, with casino games such as baccarat and blackjack adding another familiar part of the agent's world. The changing tasks give a small overhead figure several recognisably Bond-like roles.

Nintendo published the game in 1998, following the enormous success of GoldenEye on Nintendo 64. Saffire built an original portable adventure rather than attempt to reproduce that console game's perspective. Super Game Boy support added colour when played through the television accessory, while cartridge saves preserved the longer mission between sessions. The result expresses the licence through the breadth of an assignment: travel, talk, gamble, investigate and fight all belong to the same journey, allowing the handheld to represent more than a series of shooting encounters.
story_headings: The right item opens the next part of the mission
A different Bond for a different Nintendo machine
